Here’s a clear plan based on what you’ve decided.

1) Your event (locked in)
- What: Outdoor community picnic  
- Where: Public park in Darwin, NT (good shade + nearby toilets; first‑come, first‑served shelters are fine)  
- When: Sunday 14 December 2025, 9:30 am–1:30 pm  
- Size: ~30–40 people  
- Main contact: maria.gonzalez@example.com  
- Format: Short welcome at the start, then informal mingling; bring‑a‑plate style with basics provided by you.

2) Picking and using a park
When comparing parks, prioritise:
- Shade: Large trees or covered picnic shelters near open grass (for games).  
- Toilets: Within a short, flat walk; ideally visible or very close.  
- Tables/shelters: At least a couple of tables or one decent shelter; nearby grass for rugs.  
- Access: Reasonable parking and clear paths for prams/wheelchairs if possible.

Day‑of strategy for first‑come shelters:
- Arrive 1–1.5 hours early (around 8:00–8:30 am) with 1–2 helpers.  
- Bring tablecloths and a simple sign: “Community Picnic – 9:30 am–1:30 pm – All welcome.”  
- Claim the space with some chairs/rugs and your supplies while you set up.

3) Simple layout
- Food & drinks table: Under shelter/shade, away from the main running path.  
- “Welcome/info” spot: Small sign with event name, rough timings, and your name/contact.  
- Kids’ zone: On grass, with space for running and games, not blocking toilets/paths.  
- Quiet corner: A rug or a couple of chairs slightly away from the main area.

4) Checklist – what you provide (low–moderate budget)

Food & drink basics:
- Water: Large water jugs or an esky with water; cups (reusable if possible).  
- Light snacks: Fruit (e.g., watermelon, grapes, mandarins) and simple crackers/biscuits.  
- Plates, cups, napkins, cutlery: Enough for 40 plus a small buffer.  
- Serving gear: A few serving spoons/tongs, a couple of knives for fruit, paper towel.

Setup & comfort:
- 2–3 tablecloths (for food and maybe a kids’ activity table).  
- Picnic rugs/blankets and a few folding chairs.  
- Shade backup if available: small gazebo or beach umbrellas.  
- Rubbish and recycling bags, plus tape/string to attach them to a post or table.  
- Hand sanitiser and a small first‑aid kit (band‑aids, wipes, sunscreen if you can).

Kids’ activities (simple, cheap):
- Balls (soccer/footy/soft balls), frisbee.  
- Bubbles (a few bubble wands) and sidewalk chalk.  
- Optional: One or two simple organised games (e.g., relay race, treasure/scavenger hunt).

5) Simple run sheet

- 8:00–8:30 am: You + helper arrive, find/claim shelter, set up tables, sign, rubbish bags.  
- 9:30 am: Guests start arriving – greet them, direct food to the shared table.  
- 9:45 am: Short welcome/thank‑you (2–3 minutes).  
- 10:00 am onwards: Eating and informal mingling; kids’ games and bubbles available.  
- ~11:00–11:15 am (optional): One simple group game for kids.  
- 1:00 pm: Start gentle wind‑down and invite people to help tidy.  
- 1:30 pm: Finish packing up; leave the area clean.

Sample welcome wording:
“Hi everyone, thanks so much for coming today. I’m Maria, and I’m really glad we could all get together.  
This is a relaxed community picnic – please help yourselves to water and snacks, and add any food you’ve brought to the table so everyone can share.  
Kids are welcome to use the games and bubbles over there.  
We’ll just be mingling and enjoying the park until about 1:30 pm.  
Thanks again for being here, and please let me know if you need anything.”

6) Invite text you can send (email/message)

Subject: Community Picnic – Sunday 14 December, Darwin

Body:
“Hi everyone,

You’re invited to a relaxed community picnic in Darwin.

Date: Sunday 14 December 2025  
Time: 9:30 am–1:30 pm  
Location: Public park in Darwin (final park details to be confirmed – we’ll choose a spot with good shade and nearby toilets)

Format:
- Casual outdoor picnic with around 30–40 people  
- Short welcome around 9:45 am, then informal mingling  
- Kid‑friendly: space for ball games, bubbles, chalk and simple activities

Food:
- Please bring a plate of food to share (sweet or savoury – whatever you like).  
- We’ll provide water, cups, plates, napkins, and some fruit/snacks.

What to bring:
- Picnic rug or chairs if you have them  
- Sun protection (hat, sunscreen) and anything else you need to be comfortable

Main contact on the day: Maria Gonzalez – maria.gonzalez@example.com

Once we confirm the exact park, we’ll share a map pin and where to find us in the park.

Hope you can make it!”

If you’d like, I can now:
- Turn this into a shorter “calendar event description” you can paste into calendar invites, or  
- Help compare 2–3 specific parks you’re considering and tweak this plan for the one you choose.</action>

- Bring a bit of extra shade (umbrella/small gazebo) in case your chosen spot is sunnier than expected.
- Pack spare sunscreen and maybe a couple of extra hats.
- A few large garbage bags or a small tarp can protect food if there’s a brief shower.

2) Communication
- Once you lock in the exact park and spot, save a map pin and a one‑line description (“shelter near the playground / by the BBQs”) to send out.
- Have a short “We’re here / running a bit late” message ready to copy‑paste on the day.

3) Helpers & roles
- Line up 2–3 helpers in advance for:
  - Early setup and claiming the shelter.
  - Keeping the food/drink table tidy.
  - Overseeing one or two kids’ games.

4) Quick practical checks
- Double‑check park rules (BBQs, any restrictions on games, marquees, etc.).
- Think about how you’ll handle any shared costs (just you, or optional contributions).

If you tell me which park you choose later, I can help you write a very short “day‑of directions + map pin” message to send to everyone.
